EMPOWERING life-long learners
Dunton Green is a village school with a long history of being at the heart of the local community and we are proud of our friendly, happy and caring school. Each pupil is valued and encouraged to achieve to the best of their abilities.
Our goal is to ensure that all pupils follow the core values and develop a lifelong love of learning. We are committed to ensuring that our wider curriculum is exciting and enriching, in addition to high academic expectations, there is a strong emphasis on personal and social development, physical education, music and the Arts. We want every child to leave Dunton Green as a confident, curious and compassionate individual, well prepared for the next stage of their education and for life beyond school.

There is no better way to get to know Dunton Green Primary School than to come and experience it for yourself.

pageCache.text:
Our Curriculum
At Dunton Green Primary School, we provide a broad, balanced and ambitious curriculum that aims to foster a lifelong love of learning.
Our curriculum is designed to give children the knowledge, skills, experiences and confidence they need to succeed at Dunton Green and beyond. We want learning to be engaging, purposeful and memorable, while ensuring that children develop secure knowledge and understanding across the full range of subjects.
Our curriculum is based on the National Curriculum for England, the Early Years Foundation Stage statutory framework and the appropriate curriculum requirements for Religious Education.
Our curriculum aims
Through our curriculum, we want every child to:
become a confident and enthusiastic reader;
communicate effectively through speaking and writing;
develop mathematical fluency, reasoning and problem-solving skills;
become curious about the world around them;
think critically, ask questions and solve problems;
develop creativity and self-expression;
How our curriculum is organised
Learning is carefully planned and sequenced so that children's knowledge and skills develop progressively as they move through the school.
Our year-group curriculum overviews, available below, show the content children will encounter during each term and across each subject.
Teachers make meaningful connections between subjects where these help children to deepen their understanding, while ensuring that children develop the distinctive knowledge and skills associated with individual subjects.
A range of high-quality resources and curriculum programmes support our teaching. These include Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised for phonics and early reading, White Rose to support Mathematics, Kapow Primary for Music and SCARF for PSHE.
Reading and phonics
Reading is fundamental to children's success and has a high priority throughout our curriculum.
In Reception and Key Stage 1, we use Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised as our systematic synthetic phonics programme to teach children to read.
As children progress through school, they encounter a wide range of high-quality texts and develop their fluency, vocabulary, comprehension and enjoyment of reading.
An inclusive curriculum
Our curriculum is for every child.
Teachers use adaptive teaching, appropriate resources and reasonable adjustments to ensure that pupils, including those with SEND, can access ambitious learning and participate successfully in the full curriculum.
Further information about how we support pupils with SEND can be found on our Inclusion & SEND page.
Learning beyond the classroom
We believe that some of children's most memorable learning happens beyond individual lessons.
Our curriculum is enriched through educational visits, visitors to school, sporting opportunities, performances, music, clubs and other experiences.
Children have opportunities to participate in a range of sports and physical activities, including swimming, and we encourage every child to discover forms of physical activity that they enjoy.
Children also have opportunities to learn musical instruments, including through specialist and peripatetic tuition.
By the time children leave Dunton Green, we want them to have developed not only academically, but also as confident, respectful and responsible young people with positive memories of their primary education.
Religious Education
Religious Education enables children to develop their knowledge and understanding of religions and worldviews and to consider important questions about belief, meaning and how people live.
Parents and carers have a statutory right to withdraw their child from all or part of Religious Education. We encourage any parent considering withdrawal to speak to the Head of School so that the curriculum and the implications of withdrawal can be discussed.
What will my child learn?
Our curriculum overviews show what children learn across the academic year.
If you would like further information about the curriculum taught at Dunton Green, please contact the school office.

Come and See Us!
A Small School with a Big Heart
Dunton Green is a one-form-entry primary school, with up to 30 children joining us in Reception each year.
Being a smaller school means that we can really get to know our children and families. We pride ourselves on creating a friendly and inclusive community where children feel that they belong and where families are an important part of school life.
Our values of Respect, Resilience, Perseverance, Teamwork, Achievement and Kindness run through everything we do.
We want children to leave Dunton Green not only having achieved academically, but having developed confidence, curiosity, friendships and memories that will stay with them long after primary school.
Learning Beyond the Classroom
One of the things that makes Dunton Green special is the importance we place on giving children a wide range of experiences.
Our curriculum includes opportunities for outdoor learning, educational visits, visitors to school, sport, music and enrichment alongside high-quality classroom teaching.
We want our children to discover the things they love, experience new opportunities and develop the confidence to take on challenges.
By the time children leave us for secondary school, our ambition is that they are academically well-prepared, have discovered sports and activities they enjoy, have experienced music and the arts, understand and respect others, and have developed a genuine love of learning.
Nurture, Wellbeing and Belonging
Children learn best when they feel safe, happy and valued.
Pastoral care is an important part of life at Dunton Green. Our staff work hard to build strong relationships with children and families and to make sure children know that there is always an adult who knows them, listens to them and will support them.
We recognise that every child is different. Our inclusive approach means that we work closely with families to understand children's individual strengths and needs and help them to flourish.
What to Expect When You Visit
We know that choosing a school is a significant decision.
A website can tell you about our curriculum, results and policies, but it cannot quite capture the atmosphere of a school. That's why we think visiting is so important.
During your visit, you'll be able to walk around the school while it is in action, see children learning, meet members of our team and ask as many questions as you would like.
Visits usually last around 30–45 minutes, although we are very happy to spend longer with you if there is more that you would like to discuss.
Younger brothers and sisters are very welcome to come along too.
There is absolutely no obligation to apply after your visit. We simply want you to have the opportunity to see Dunton Green for yourself and decide whether it feels like the right school for your child and your family.
Looking for a Reception Place?
We welcome up to 30 children into Reception each September.
If your child is due to start school, we would particularly encourage you to visit during a normal school day. You'll be able to see what learning looks like, meet our team and find out how we help children make the important transition into primary school.
Choosing your child's first school is a big milestone, and we want you to feel completely comfortable asking us anything.
Moving School or New to the Area?
Children join Dunton Green throughout the school year for all sorts of reasons.
If you're moving into Dunton Green or Sevenoaks, or you're considering whether another school might better meet your child's needs, you're equally welcome to arrange a visit.
We can talk to you about availability in the year group you need, show you around and explain how we support children joining us part-way through their primary education.
Come and Discover Dunton Green
The best way to decide whether Dunton Green is the right school for your family is simply to come and meet us.
We would be delighted to show you around.

Contact the school office to arrange a visit at a time that works for you.

Why Choose Us?

Admissions
We are delighted that you are considering Dunton Green Primary School for your child.
Dunton Green Primary School is a community primary school. Kent County Council is the admission authority for the school and is responsible for determining the school's admission arrangements.
If you would like to visit us before making an application, please see our Come and See Us! page or contact the school office. We would be very pleased to show you around.
Starting school in Reception
Children are normally admitted to Reception in the September following their fourth birthday.
Applications for Reception places are made through the local authority where you live. For families living in Kent, applications should be made through Kent County Council's Primary School Admissions service.
Kent County Council publishes the application timetable, admission arrangements and oversubscription criteria for community and voluntary controlled schools each year.
For children starting Reception in September 2027, applications should be made through Kent County Council's primary admissions process.
The school's Published Admission Number (PAN) is 30 pupils for each year group.
How places are allocated
As a community school, Dunton Green Primary School does not set its own oversubscription criteria.
Where there are more applications than places available, Kent County Council applies its published admission arrangements and oversubscription criteria for community and voluntary controlled primary schools.
Full details of the current criteria and how they are applied can be found on the Kent County Council website.
Children with an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) that names Dunton Green Primary School are admitted through the statutory EHCP process rather than through the normal oversubscription arrangements.
Deferred entry and part-time attendance
Children are entitled to a full-time Reception place from the September following their fourth birthday.
Parents may request that their child starts school later in the school year, provided that the place is taken up before the child reaches compulsory school age and within the academic year for which the place was offered.
Parents may also request that their child attends part-time until they reach compulsory school age.
If you would like to discuss deferred entry or part-time attendance, please contact the school office.
Further information about school starting age is available from Kent County Council.
Summer-born children
Parents of children born between 1 April and 31 August may, in certain circumstances, request admission to Reception outside their child's normal age group.
Requests are considered in accordance with Kent County Council's admission arrangements and the Department for Education's guidance.
Parents considering this option are encouraged to contact Kent County Council and the school as early as possible to discuss their child's circumstances.
In-year admissions
If you would like your child to join Dunton Green Primary School after the start of Reception, or at any point during Years 1 to 6, this is known as an in-year admission.
Parents should complete a Kent County Council In-Year Admissions Form (IYAF) and send the completed form directly to the school.
You are very welcome to contact us before applying. We can tell you whether there is currently space in the relevant year group, arrange a visit and talk to you about how we support children joining us during the school year.
However, availability can change and a place can only be formally offered following receipt and consideration of an application.
Completed forms can be returned to:
Dunton Green Primary School London Road Dunton Green Sevenoaks Kent TN13 2UP
Email: office@dunton-green.kent.sch.uk
Telephone: 01732 462221
Waiting lists
Where a year group is full, applications will be considered in accordance with Kent County Council's admission arrangements.
Information about waiting lists, including how long they are maintained and how places are prioritised, can be found within Kent County Council's current admission arrangements.
Parents should be aware that a child's position on a waiting list can change as new applications are received, because places are prioritised according to the published oversubscription criteria rather than the date on which an application was made.
Admission appeals
Parents have a legal right to appeal if their child is refused a place at Dunton Green Primary School.
Appeals are arranged in accordance with the statutory School Admission Appeals Code.
For Reception applications made as part of the normal admissions round, Kent County Council publishes an annual appeals timetable.
For in-year applications, information about appealing will be provided if a place cannot be offered.
Children with an Education, Health and Care Plan
Applications for children with an Education, Health and Care Plan are managed through the statutory SEND process rather than the usual school admissions process.
Parents should contact their local authority SEND team regarding the naming of a school within an EHCP.
Further information for Kent families is available through Kent County Council's SEND services and the Kent Local Offer.
Moving into the area
Families move to Dunton Green and the surrounding area throughout the year and we are always happy to hear from prospective families.
If you are moving into the area, please contact us. We can discuss current availability, arrange a tour and help you understand the in-year application process.
Please do not remove your child from their existing school until a new school place has been confirmed.
Come and visit us
Choosing a school is an important decision and we think the best way to understand Dunton Green is to come and see us.
You can meet our staff, see the children learning and get a feel for our friendly, welcoming school.
Alternatively, contact the school office on 01732 462221 or email office@dunton-green.kent.sch.uk to arrange a visit.
Further information
For full and current information about school admissions, including application dates, admission criteria, waiting lists and appeals, please visit the Kent County Council School Admissions website.
Kent County Council is the admission authority for Dunton Green Primary School.
Joining Us

Learning
At Dunton Green, we want every child to develop the knowledge, skills, confidence and curiosity they need to succeed at school and in later life.
We provide a broad, balanced and ambitious curriculum that is carefully planned so that children’s learning builds progressively from Reception to Year 6. Reading is at the heart of our curriculum, alongside strong foundations in writing and mathematics and meaningful learning across the full range of subjects.
Our teachers bring learning to life through high-quality teaching, carefully chosen texts, practical experiences, educational visits, visitors, sport, music, creativity and opportunities to learn beyond the classroom. Teaching is adapted so that every child, including those with SEND, can participate successfully and experience challenge and achievement.
The pages below provide more information about our curriculum, Reception and Early Years, reading and phonics, individual subjects, classes and the wider opportunities that help make learning at Dunton Green memorable.

Safeguarding
Keeping children safe at Dunton Green
At Dunton Green Primary School, the safety and wellbeing of every child is our highest priority.
We are committed to providing a safe, caring and supportive environment in which children can learn, develop and flourish. Everyone who works at, visits or volunteers at our school has a responsibility to help keep children safe.
Safeguarding is everyone's responsibility.
We work closely with children, families and other professionals to:
provide a safe and secure environment for children;
help children understand how to keep themselves and others safe;
identify children who may need additional help or support;
recognise and respond to concerns about abuse, neglect or exploitation;
take prompt and appropriate action when we are concerned about a child's welfare; and
work in partnership with other agencies to safeguard and promote the welfare of children.
Our safeguarding arrangements are informed by statutory guidance, including Keeping Children Safe in Education and Working Together to Safeguard Children.
Our Safeguarding Team
If you have a concern about the safety or welfare of a child, please speak to a member of our safeguarding team.
Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL) Daisy Holliday - Head of School
Deputy Designated Safeguarding Leads (DDSLs) Justine Hennessy - Family Liaison Officer Sarah Norsworthy - Assistant Head of School Ben Hulme - Executive Headteacher Safeguarding Governor Hilary Wilder
You can contact the school safeguarding team through the school office:
Telephone: 01732 462221 Email: office@dunton-green.kent.sch.uk
If you are worried about a child, please tell us. No concern is too small to share.
What should I do if I am worried about a child?
If you are concerned about something you have seen or heard, or about a change in a child's appearance, behaviour or wellbeing, please speak to the Designated Safeguarding Lead or one of the Deputy Designated Safeguarding Leads as soon as possible.
You do not need to be certain that a child is being harmed before raising a concern.
If a child tells you something that concerns you:
listen carefully and take them seriously;
remain calm and reassuring;
do not promise to keep what they tell you a secret;
do not investigate or ask leading questions;
explain that you will need to share the information with someone who can help;
record the concern accurately; and
report it immediately in accordance with the school's safeguarding procedures.
If you believe a child is in immediate danger, call 999.
Concerns outside school
You do not have to contact the school before reporting a safeguarding concern.
If you are worried that a child may be at risk of harm, you can contact Kent Children's Social Care directly.
Kent Children's Social Care: 03000 41 11 11 Monday to Friday, 9am–5pm
Out of hours: 03000 41 91 91
If a child is in immediate danger, always call 999.
Concerns about an adult working with children
We take all concerns about the conduct of adults working or volunteering in school seriously.
If you have a concern about the behaviour of a member of staff, volunteer or another adult working with children at Dunton Green, you should report this to the Head of School as soon as possible.
If the concern relates to the Head of School, it should be reported to the Executive Headteacher.
If the concern relates to the Executive Headteacher, it should be reported to the Chair of Governors.
Concerns will be managed in accordance with statutory safeguarding guidance and, where appropriate, advice will be sought from the Local Authority Designated Officer (LADO).
Online Safety
Technology is an important part of children's learning and their lives. We teach children how to use technology safely, responsibly and respectfully and how to seek help when something online makes them worried or uncomfortable.
Online safeguarding includes protecting children from risks relating to:
contact with other people;
their own or others' online conduct; and
online commercial risks.
The school has appropriate filtering and monitoring systems in place to help protect children when using school technology and internet-connected devices. These arrangements are reviewed regularly as part of our wider safeguarding responsibilities.
We also work with parents and carers to help children develop safe and healthy habits when using technology at home and at school.
If you are concerned about something that has happened online, please speak to a member of our safeguarding team.
Child-on-child abuse
Children can sometimes cause harm to other children.
We recognise that child-on-child abuse can take many forms, including bullying, physical abuse, sexual harassment, sexual violence, harmful sexual behaviour and abuse that takes place online.
We do not dismiss harmful behaviour as 'banter', 'part of growing up' or 'just having a laugh'.
Children are encouraged to speak to a trusted adult whenever something makes them feel unsafe or uncomfortable. All concerns are taken seriously and responded to appropriately.
Preventing radicalisation
Protecting children from the risk of radicalisation and extremism forms part of our wider safeguarding responsibilities.
We help children develop the knowledge and skills they need to think critically, understand different perspectives, challenge prejudice and keep themselves safe.
Staff are trained to recognise and respond to concerns that a child may be vulnerable to radicalisation. Any such concerns are managed through our established safeguarding procedures and, where necessary, in partnership with other agencies.
Attendance and safeguarding
Regular school attendance is important for children's education, wellbeing and safety.
We recognise that changes in attendance, patterns of absence or children missing education can sometimes be indicators of wider safeguarding concerns.
We therefore monitor attendance carefully and work with children and families to understand and address barriers to regular attendance.
Where necessary, we work with other agencies to ensure children receive the right help and support.
Operation Encompass
Dunton Green Primary School is part of Operation Encompass.
Operation Encompass is a partnership between schools and the police that helps schools provide timely support to children who have experienced or been exposed to domestic abuse.
Where the police attend an incident of domestic abuse involving a child connected with our school, relevant information may be shared securely with trained members of our safeguarding team before the start of the next school day.
This enables us to provide appropriate support and understanding for the child when they arrive at school.
Information received through Operation Encompass is treated sensitively and confidentially and is managed in accordance with our safeguarding procedures.
Safer recruitment and visitors
We follow statutory safer recruitment procedures when appointing staff and engaging volunteers.
Appropriate checks are undertaken according to the role being carried out, including Disclosure and Barring Service checks where required.
All visitors must report to the school office, sign in and follow the school's safeguarding and visitor procedures while on site.
Visitors must wear the identification provided by the school and must not take photographs or recordings of children unless specifically authorised to do so.
Helping children to keep themselves safe
Safeguarding is embedded throughout school life and our curriculum.
We teach children, in an age-appropriate way, about:
healthy and respectful relationships;
recognising unsafe or worrying situations;
boundaries and consent;
bullying and discrimination;
personal safety; and
how and when to speak up.
We want every child at Dunton Green to know that there are adults who will listen to them, take them seriously and help them.
Working with families
Strong relationships with parents and carers are an important part of keeping children safe.
We aim to work openly and constructively with families and will usually discuss concerns with parents or carers.
There may, however, be circumstances where we need to seek advice or make a referral to another agency before speaking to a parent or carer, particularly where doing so could place a child at greater risk or compromise a safeguarding investigation.
Our first consideration will always be the safety and welfare of the child.
